notes.meaning: David commands his own inner being to praise the Lord. True worship is not just reciting words, but putting the whole heart, mind, and soul into honoring God. We praise Him because of who He is and His complete goodness.

David tells himself again to praise God and never to forget all the kind things the Lord has done. People easily overlook God's daily goodness when life feels routine or difficult. Keeping a thankful memory helps our hearts stay close to Him.

Pardon for sin is the greatest benefit, and David names it first. God washes away all our guilt and brings restoration to broken lives. When our sins are forgiven, the wall separating us from God's favor is taken away.

differ.view: Many teach that 'diseases' here refers primarily to spiritual sickness, meaning the corruption and damage of sin that God heals in the soul.
Many teach that this promise includes real, physical healing for the body in this life.

notes.meaning: God rescues believers from the grave and from eternal ruin. He does not stop at saving them from death, but also crowns them with tender mercy and loyal love, treating them like honored royalty.
The Lord fills our lives with good things that truly satisfy the heart. He restores our strength so that, like an eagle soaring with fresh vigor, we have new energy to live and serve Him.
David looks beyond his own life to God's care for all people who suffer. The Lord stands up as a fair judge for those who are mistreated, bringing justice to the helpless and oppressed.

God revealed His character and purposes directly to Moses and displayed His mighty acts to the nation of Israel. Moses was allowed to understand God's heart and ways, while the people witnessed His miracles of rescue.

The Lord is full of tender compassion, deeply kind, and very slow to become angry. This repeats the famous words God spoke about Himself to Moses at Mount Sinai, showing that mercy is central to who He is.
God disciplines His children when they wander, but He does not stay angry or hold a grudge forever. When a person turns from wrongdoing, God's correction gives way to warm restoration.
God does not treat us as harshly as our wrongs deserve. If the Lord gave us the full penalty for our sins, none of us could survive. We live each day under His patient restraint.
The immense height of the sky above the earth shows that God's love has no limit. This boundless mercy is promised to those who fear Him, which means respecting Him with holy awe and trust.
East and west can never meet, and that picture shows how thoroughly God carries away our guilt. When He pardons our sins, He removes them so far that they can never return to condemn us.

The Lord treats those who revere Him with the same gentle care that a loving father shows to his children. He understands our fears and struggles, looking upon our weakness with pity rather than disgust.
God knows how fragile we are because He formed us from the dust of the ground. Because He remembers our physical and moral weakness, He deals with us gently instead of crushing us.
Human life is brief and fragile, like grass and flowers growing in an open field. A hot wind blows over them, and they vanish so quickly that the place where they grew retains no memory of them.

Human life quickly fades, but God's faithful love lasts from everlasting to everlasting. This generational blessing belongs to those who honor Him, keep His sacred agreement, and carefully follow His commands.
The Lord sits on a secure throne in heaven that can never be shaken. His royal authority governs every creature and event in the universe, assuring His people that His promises will always stand.
David invites the powerful angels in heaven to join in the chorus of praise. These mighty messengers listen eagerly for God's voice and carry out His commands with joyful obedience.
All the heavenly armies and servants of God are called to give Him honor. Every created power that carries out His good pleasure owes Him constant praise and adoration.
Everything God has created across His vast universe is summoned to praise Him. David then brings the song back to where it began, urging his own heart to personally bless the Lord.
